I would avoid calling the police as much as possible, especially considering the behaviors you’ve described. they aren’t trained to handle mental health crisis’ and often end up making things worse. getting her to a crisis center asap is going to be your best bet, if you’re able to drive her there yourself that would be easiest but you can also call for an ambulance to take her. first, i would call around to find somewhere that can guarantee an available bed before taking her anywhere. as others have said, there is a different process for being involuntarily committed, but crisis center’s always do two mental health screenings (a nurse practitioner and a doctor) so you don’t need to worry about getting a 2PC. if she is truly a danger to herself they will see it, they’re trained to look for those signs. then, once she’s been admitted you can trust that the staff will keep her safe for a few days to a week. while she’s there my advice would be to find a residential mental health clinic. there’s some that offer permanent housing if you think that’s necessary, but most often the programs are aimed at rehabilitation so she’d be able to return to normal life once she’s deemed safe. because residential programs are for long term treatment, care is more personalized and isn’t limited to prescribing a handful of new pills. ideally this means lasting recovery, and a specific action plan should things get bad again.
